title: kv-cache: improved memory management and eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation, paging, and spillover
author: Ayesha Patel
description:
Motivation: Large, long-running sessions expose fragmentation and suboptimal eviction behavior in the KV cache which causes increased device-to-host paging and spillover under high-concurrency workloads. This manifests as elevated p99 token latency and transient OOMs on pods running tight GPU memory budgets. Goal: improve memory utilization, reduce fragmentation, and implement predictable spillover thresholds so production workloads maintain latency SLOs without increasing reserved capacity.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a lightweight slab tracking layer to track free/used chunks inside the KV cache to reduce per-key fragmentation. 2) Add a background compaction/defragmentation pass that opportunistically coalesces adjacent free spans when the GPU is underutilized. 3) Implement a tiered spillover policy: (a) soft_spill_threshold triggers asynchronous eviction to host pinned memory, (b) hard_spill_threshold triggers synchronous spill to host and evicts least-recently-used spans. 4) Replace the global eviction timer with a scoring-based eviction policy that accounts for key size, access recency, and affinity to active batch lanes. 5) Expose runtime knobs and telemetry: kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv_cache.spill_count, kv_cache.compaction_runs, and a new tracing span for spill events. 6) Add tests and benchmarks demonstrating end-to-end improvements and guardrails for config changes.

Design notes: - Slab allocator: we kept the allocator API backward compatible; the slab layer only changes how free extents are selected and coalesced. It introduces a compact metadata array per allocation region to limit memory overhead. - Compaction: runs in a low-priority worker thread pinned to a dedicated CPU core; compaction is rate-limited to avoid interfering with inference. Compaction is disabled by default for low-tier Dedicated customers; enabled for Hosted and high-commit Dedicated by rollout flag. - Spillover semantics: soft_spill is async and attempts to preserve KV entries for warm prefixes; hard_spill is synchronous and prioritized during memory pressure to prevent OOM. Both paths are audited and instrumented. - Eviction scoring: score = w_recency * recency_rank + w_size * normalized_size + w_lane_affinity * lane_score. We tuned weights from telemetry and included a safe default.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks and canary runs on a rtx-a6000-like instance show: - 18% reduction in average KV memory overhead across mixed-length chat traces. - p99 latency improvement of 7-12% on long-context workloads (32k tokens) in our perf-canary harness. - Paging/spill events reduced by ~62% under bursty traffic in the Dedicated staging fleet. - No statistically significant regression in cold-start latency. See commits for raw perf data and perf harness scripts.

Compatibility and rollout: Changes are behind two feature flags: KV_CACHE_SLAB_ENABLED and KV_CACHE_COMPACTION_ENABLED. Default rollout: slab enabled for all clusters immediately; compaction off by default and enabled progressively via console rollouts. We added a migration that records pre-upgrade fragmentation metrics; no data transformation is required.

Testing and CI: added unit tests for slab allocation and eviction scoring, integration tests for spill paths using the mock host-store, and end-to-end canary jobs in perf-canary. CI includes new benchmark-run job; one historical flaky test was stabilized in this PR.

Files of interest: src/runtime/kv_cache/allocator.cc; src/runtime/kv_cache/eviction_policy.cc; src/runtime/kv_cache/compactor.cc; include/kv_cache/config.h; tools/perf/canary/kv_spillover_test.py; docs/kv-cache.md.

Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout, monitor kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio and kv_cache.spill_count per-region; rollback plan disables slab and compaction and reverts eviction scoring via config if regressions observed.

release_notes:
- Improve KV cache memory utilization by adding slab allocation and background compaction.
- New tiered spillover policy to reduce device-to-host paging and transient OOMs.
- Expose telemetry and runtime knobs for fragmentation, spill counts, and compaction.
- Performance: reduced p99 latency on long-context workloads and fewer spill events under bursty traffic.
